deltaNote: ICJ set the merits-phase timetable Aug 6, 2026; oral hearings would begin in early 2029 with judgment roughly six months later if the schedule holds — a multi-year process despite the June admissibility ruling.

label: Washington Accords status
delta: Seventh JSCM session opened Sept 16, 2026 in Geneva, running through Sept 17, ahead of an October trilateral planning conference
deltaNote: DRC and M23 agreed a sequenced roadmap after Aug 17-21 Geneva talks; the first EJVM+ verification mission then deployed to Minembwe on Aug 24, but DRC accused M23 of killing 300+ people in June-July and M23 accused government forces of an artillery attack near Minembwe, signalling the mechanism has yet to reduce mutual distrust. At an Aug 12-13 JSCM session, DRC and Rwanda agreed to advance two initiatives to strengthen on-the-ground monitoring and verification, and DRC presented its FDLR DDR plan; the seventh JSCM meeting opened Sept 16, 2026 in Geneva (through Sept 17) with US, Qatar, Togo and AU mediation, feeding into an October trilateral planning conference. Rwanda has rejected DRC's July 28 disarmament protocol with an FDLR faction, insisting on neutralization rather than negotiated disarmament and conditioning its own defensive-posture rollback on the group's dismantlement — talks opened even as fighting continued in Masisi, Walikale and Fizi.

label: Doha comprehensive peace deal target
contestNote: An Aug 22, 2026 roadmap set sequenced negotiation steps, but M23 has made no firm disarmament commitments and fighting widened across Fizi, Minembwe, Kalehe, Masisi and Walungu even as the roadmap was signed

label: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak deaths
contestNote: Congolese health experts say the true toll may be several times higher than confirmed figures, since the outbreak — declared May 15, 2026 in Ituri — spread undetected for weeks beforehand.
delta: 7,820 confirmed cases as of the Sept 25, 2026 Africa CDC update; North Kivu's caseload has overtaken Ituri's
deltaNote: Deaths passed the 3,000 mark for the first time on Sept 2 (3,007 deaths/6,186 cases); by Sept 25 Africa CDC data the toll had risen to 3,779 deaths among 7,820 confirmed cases (~48% case-fatality rate) across 63 health zones in seven provinces. Regional trends have diverged sharply: over the latest three-week period Ituri (the epicenter) saw cases fall 25% and deaths drop 31%, while North Kivu's caseload rose 56% and deaths there climbed 19%, giving North Kivu the highest case-fatality ratio nationally at ~60.5%. About 65% of cases are still first identified within communities rather than through surveillance. An Ervebo vaccine clinical trial targeting 20,000 people, testing efficacy against the Bundibugyo strain, began in Bunia on Sept 19. Now DRC's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak's 3,317 cases, and the second-largest globally.
